To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce a new graph convolution, second-order graph convolution, that is a maximally localized spectral kernel, 2) we build purely topological graph convolutional networks based on SoGC and demonstrate that they consistently achieve state-of-the-art results on the latest benchmark, and 3) we introduce GRU into spectral GCNs and further improve our experimental results.

(i) SoGCN achieves state-of-the-arts on all benchmark datasets; (ii) SoGCN is a general-purpose model that can be applied to various tasks, including node classification and graph generation; (iii) SoGCN can be used to build graph generative model, and (iv) SoGCN has the potential to be used as a general-purpose graph model for various tasks.

(i) SoGC can be viewed as a maximally localized spectral graph kernel, (ii) SoGC can form the basic building block for graph convolutional networks, and (iii) SoGC can achieve state-of-the-art classification performance on graph classification benchmarks.
